title: AI Operating Model and Center of Excellence: From Pilots to Platform (2026)

questions.question: What maturity result does score_readiness return when only funded_team is present?
options: 0/100 and AD_HOC, because one signal cannot establish maturity
70/100 and DIFFERENTIATED, because a funded team owns every platform concern
25/100 and OPPORTUNISTIC, with a recommendation to enforce standards in CI
45/100 and SYSTEMATIC, because funding implies operating cadence
questions.explanation: funded_team contributes weight 25. That clears the 20-point OPPORTUNISTIC threshold, whose next step is moving written standards into CI enforcement.

questions.question: Which absent signal does highest_leverage_next_signal choose for the sample organization?
options: governance_cadence, because cadence is the first missing operating ritual
champion_network, because champions own all delivery work
asset_library_active, because libraries always outrank standards
standards_enforced, because its absent weight 25 is the largest available jump
questions.explanation: The sample has only funded_team. Among absent signals, standards_enforced also weighs 25, which is higher than the asset library and champion network at 20 and cadence at 10.

questions.question: What changes when standards_enforced is activated in the sample?
options: The score becomes 50 and the maturity level becomes SYSTEMATIC
The level remains OPPORTUNISTIC because standards are not an organizational signal
The level jumps to TRANSFORMATIONAL because two signals are sufficient
The score becomes 25 and the level becomes AD_HOC because signals do not add
questions.explanation: Funding contributes 25 and standards enforcement adds another 25, producing 50. The threshold table maps 50 to SYSTEMATIC, whose recommendation is to activate the champion network.

questions.question: Who owns 'Adjust sprint priorities within approved cost envelope'?
options: CoE Platform, because every AI backlog decision is a platform standard
Delivery Team, because scope changes stay within an approved envelope and do not change standards
Joint, because any delivery change needs portfolio funding
Joint, because no owner can decide within a cost envelope
questions.explanation: route_decision sends non-portfolio delivery-scope changes that do not affect standards to Owner.DELIVERY_TEAM. The team owns the reprioritisation within the approved boundary.

questions.question: Where does route_decision send a prompt-injection security incident?
options: Delivery Team only, because incidents are implementation work
The monthly portfolio review, because incidents cannot change standards
CoE Platform first, with the delivery team executing the fix under its direction
Joint without a designated DRI, because security boundaries are shared
questions.explanation: is_security_incident is checked first. The CoE updates the platform standard and directs the delivery team, keeping one accountable platform owner while implementation proceeds.

questions.question: What owner and control does route_decision return for 'Fund a new use case'?
options: Delivery Team, with no portfolio review because the use case is new
CoE Platform only, because business-unit budget requests cannot affect delivery
Joint without a tie-breaker, because shared ownership is the final control
Joint (needs single DRI), because portfolio funding touches CoE priorities and delivery scope
questions.explanation: The decision is portfolio-level and affects delivery scope, so the router returns Owner.JOINT and explicitly requires a single DRI, typically the CoE lead.
